methodology.title: Measurement methodology
methodology.intro: Our figures are measured on real published trades, never invented. Here is exactly how.
methodology.definitionBody: A trade is a win if its first take-profit (TP1) is reached before the stop-loss.
methodology.flatTitle: What about a trade that hits nothing?
methodology.flatBody: A trade that reaches neither take-profit nor stop before its validity ends is valued at the closing price: a small gain or a small loss depending on direction.
methodology.granularityBody: Measured on the hourly (H1) candles actually recorded.
methodology.tieBreakTitle: If target and stop are hit in the same hour?
methodology.tieBreakBody: If a single hour touches both the target and the stop, the level closest to the entry price is considered reached first.
methodology.metricsBody: Average R is the mean performance of winning trades, expressed in multiples of risk (R). Expectancy is the mean performance of ALL trades, winners and losers alike — the real expected value per trade.
methodology.periodsBody: Two windows are available: the entire measured history, and the last 90 days.
methodology.thresholdBody: No percentage is shown until the sample reaches 30 closed trades. Below that, we simply show the number of trades.
